attempts.raw_response: The dispute centres on plans to transfer production to overseas facilities, which the union claims would result in significant job losses across the site. Workers voted overwhelmingly in favour of industrial action last month after months of failed talks with management. The company has insisted the relocation is necessary to remain competitive in an increasingly challenging global market. Unite has called for urgent government intervention, urging ministers to facilitate fresh discussions between both parties. Local politicians have also expressed concern about the economic impact on the surrounding community, where the factory is one of the largest employers. Further strike dates are expected to be announced in the coming days if no resolution is reached.

pair.human_continuation: "It is vitally important that the government and MPs make it entirely clear to Rolls-Royce that its actions are deplorable and should be reversed immediately." A spokeswoman for Rolls-Royce said the company "always have a shutdown of UK facilities over Christmas" and were closing down earlier as staff "are planning to be on strike from the end of this month". "Due to the length of the industrial action and unclear duration, we will have to source parts that would normally be made in Barnoldswick from other parts of our supply chain. "This temporary use of dual source suppliers is needed to protect Rolls-Royce customers and is not the same as moving work overseas."
pair.prefix: The union said it had not agreed to the furlough scheme and was considering legal action to ensure workers who were not on strike receive 100% of their wages after the factory closes on Friday. "At a time when they should be entering into negotiations, they have instead locked workers out and moved work abroad," he said.
